attrs.title: Signs your TikTok tracking is missing sales
attrs.lead: TikTok can’t learn from sales it can’t see. These are the problems we find most often.

items.title: TikTok shows far fewer sales than your store
items.text:
Many TikTok users buy inside the app’s own browser, where the Pixel often loses track. Blockers and iPhone settings hide more. TikTok then under-reports your sales and optimises on half the data.

We add the Events API, which sends purchases from your store or server. With the Pixel and the Events API together, TikTok sees far more of your real sales.

items.title: You optimise for clicks because purchases don’t show
items.text:
When TikTok sees only a handful of purchases a week, it can’t optimise for them, so many stores fall back to clicks or add to cart, and pay for traffic that doesn’t buy.

Once purchases are tracked properly, campaigns can optimise for complete payments, and later for value, so TikTok looks for buyers, not browsers.

items.title: Purchases are counted twice
items.text:
With both the Pixel and the Events API on, every purchase arrives twice. Without the same event ID, TikTok counts both, and your results look far better than they are.

We send one event ID with both versions of each event, so TikTok keeps one. Then we compare TikTok’s purchases with your orders.

items.title: Events stopped after a site change
items.text:
A new theme, checkout app or cookie banner can remove TikTok events without anyone noticing, while campaigns keep spending.

We rebuild the events on the current site, test them, and set an alert if purchases stop arriving.

items.title: No values sent with purchases
items.text:
Without value and currency, TikTok can count sales but not revenue. You can’t see return on ad spend, and value-based bidding isn’t possible.

We send value, currency, content IDs and quantities with every purchase, matched to your product catalogue, so TikTok reports revenue and can bid for it.

items.title: Only the Pixel is installed
items.text:
Many stores installed the Pixel when they started on TikTok and never added the Events API. It’s often a few settings away in Shopify, and a small build elsewhere.

We connect the Events API through your platform, a partner integration or server-side Tag Manager, deduplicate it and test it on real purchases.

attrs.label: How we set it up
attrs.html:
How we set it up

First a call, then five steps. Ready in about a week.

A call back within 24 hours

Tell us about your store. A tracking specialist calls you back within one working day to look at your TikTok setup with you, before any work starts.

  • A real person
  • No obligation
  • Plain English

  1. We look at your Pixel, events and data in TikTok Events Manager, and compare TikTok’s purchases with your store.

    You get: A list of what’s missing, broken or counted twice.

    • Every event and its source
    • Values and content IDs
    • Deduplication and match data
    • TikTok vs store numbers

  2. We agree which events to send, from where and with which data, and how your cookie banner affects them.

    You get: An event plan you approve before we build.

    • Events and their values
    • Pixel, Events API or both
    • Customer data and consent
    • Catalogue and content IDs

  3. Our developer connects the Events API through Shopify, a partner integration or server-side Tag Manager, with event IDs for deduplication.

    You get: Both sides sending the same events.

    • Pixel events cleaned up
    • Events API connected
    • Event IDs on both sides
    • Values, currency and content IDs

  4. We place test purchases on desktop, iPhone and inside the TikTok app, then check each one in Events Manager.

    You get: Every event passed, or fixed and tested again.

    • Test purchases
    • Desktop, iPhone and in-app browser
    • Deduplication and values
    • TikTok vs store compared

  5. You get a test report and a walkthrough call. We check again after two weeks, and help you move campaigns to purchase goals.

    You get: Tracking ready for purchase-optimised campaigns.

    • A test report
    • A walkthrough call
    • An alert if purchases stop
    • A two-week check

What we set up

Eight parts of TikTok tracking, set up and tested

For each one: why it matters, what we set up, what we usually find and what you get.

Area 1 of 8

Pixel events

The Pixel sees browsing on your site and sends events quickly. It just misses too much on its own.

What we set up

  • Base code on every page
  • Standard events
  • Event parameters
  • One Pixel per business
  • Advanced matching
  • Test events

What we usually find

  • ! Two Pixels from two different apps
  • ! Complete payment firing on page reload
  • ! Custom events instead of standard ones
  • ! Events from an old theme

What you get

  • One clean Pixel
  • Standard events in the right places
  • Parameters on every event
  • Old events removed

Area 2 of 8

Events API

The Events API sends events from your store or server, so the in-app browser, blockers and short cookies don’t hide them.

What we set up

  • Shopify TikTok channel
  • Partner integrations
  • Server-side Tag Manager
  • Access token
  • Events sent from the server
  • Error checks

What we usually find

  • ! Events API never switched on
  • ! Only page views sent
  • ! An expired access token
  • ! Errors nobody looked at

What you get

  • The right connection for your platform
  • Key events sent from the server
  • Errors checked and fixed
  • An alert if events stop

Area 3 of 8

Deduplication

With the Pixel and the Events API both on, every event arrives twice. A shared event ID tells TikTok it’s the same one.

What we set up

  • Event ID on Pixel events
  • Same ID on server events
  • Matching event names
  • Timing
  • Deduplication check
  • Purchases vs orders

What we usually find

  • ! No event IDs
  • ! Different IDs on each side

  • One event ID shared by both

  • Deduplication checked
  • Purchases that match your orders

Area 4 of 8

Values and catalogue

Values turn purchases into revenue, and content IDs link sales to products in your catalogue for shopping ads.

What we set up

  • Value and currency
  • Content IDs and type
  • Quantity
  • Catalogue match
  • Discounts and shipping
  • Refunds

What we usually find

  • ! No value on purchases
  • ! Content IDs that don’t match the catalogue
  • ! Values including shipping and tax
  • ! Currency missing

What you get

  • Values on every purchase
  • Content IDs that match the catalogue
  • Values defined the same way as your reports
  • Currency on every event

Area 5 of 8

Match data

TikTok matches events to people with hashed customer data and its click ID. More matches mean better targeting and reporting.

What we set up

  • Hashed email and phone
  • External ID
  • TikTok click ID (ttclid)
  • Browser cookie (_ttp)
  • IP and user agent
  • Consent

What we usually find

  • ! No customer data sent
  • ! Click ID lost on the way to checkout
  • ! Email sent unhashed
  • ! Data sent without consent

What you get

  • Hashed customer data with every event
  • Click ID kept through checkout
  • Consent respected
  • Higher match rates

Area 6 of 8

Consent and privacy

Tracking must follow your cookie banner and privacy laws, or events go missing in some markets and break the rules in others.

What we set up

  • Cookie banner
  • Which events need consent
  • Hashing before sending
  • Limited data use
  • Privacy policy
  • Country rules

What we usually find

  • ! The Pixel firing before consent
  • ! The banner blocking all events
  • ! Unhashed data sent
  • ! Privacy policy not mentioning TikTok

What you get

  • Events that follow your banner
  • Data hashed before it leaves your site
  • A privacy policy that covers it
  • Settings checked for each market

Area 7 of 8

Campaign goals

Good tracking only helps if campaigns use it. Once purchases flow in, campaigns can optimise for them.

What we set up

  • Optimisation event
  • Purchase volume per week
  • Value-based goals
  • Attribution window
  • Catalogue and shopping ads
  • Reporting columns

What we usually find

  • ! Campaigns optimising for clicks
  • ! Too few purchases to optimise
  • ! Attribution settings never checked
  • ! Reports without revenue

What you get

  • Campaigns moved to complete payment
  • Value goals when there’s enough data
  • Attribution set and explained
  • Reports with revenue and return on ad spend

Area 8 of 8

Testing and monitoring

Tracking that isn’t tested is a guess, and tracking that isn’t watched breaks with the next site change.

What we set up

  • Test events tool
  • Desktop, iPhone and in-app browser

  • Alerts if events stop
  • A two-week check

What we usually find

  • ! Never tested after setup
  • ! Nobody checks Events Manager
  • ! Site changes break events silently
  • ! Numbers never compared with the store

What you get

  • Every event tested and recorded
  • TikTok compared with your store

Need something more custom?

Not every store fits the standard TikTok app. If your setup is unusual, tell us what you need. We’ll get on a call, understand the requirement and send you a written quote. Here are custom Events API projects we’ve built for other clients.

  • Custom-built or headless stores

    A store built on its own code, or a headless storefront with a separate checkout, where the TikTok app doesn’t work.

    What we built: Purchase and checkout events sent from the backend through the Events API, with event IDs matched to the Pixel.

    • Next.js
    • Laravel
    • Shopify Hydrogen

  • TikTok Shop and your website together

    Sales split between TikTok Shop and your own store, so neither report shows the full picture.

    What we built: Website and TikTok Shop sales reported side by side, with the website events set up so campaigns can optimise for both.

    • TikTok Shop
    • Shopify
    • Reporting

  • Subscriptions and repeat orders

    Subscription or repeat-order brands where the first purchase is only the start.

    What we built: First orders with a predicted value, and renewals sent from payment webhooks, so TikTok values customers properly.

    • Stripe
    • Recharge
    • Webhooks

  • Leads, bookings and offline sales

    Businesses that sell through forms, bookings or a sales team rather than a checkout.

    What we built: Leads matched to CRM outcomes, with qualified and won stages sent back through the Events API.

    • HubSpot
    • Zoho
    • Booking systems

  • Several brands, countries or Pixels

    One platform running several brands or markets, each with its own Pixel and ad account.

    What we built: Events routed to the right Pixel by brand or country, from one server setup that is easy to maintain.

    • Multi-brand
    • Multi-country
    • Server-side Tag Manager

  • Creator and affiliate sales

    Sales driven by creators and affiliate codes that TikTok can’t connect to campaigns.

    What we built: Discount codes and creator links passed with purchase events, so creator sales show up in reporting.

attrs.title: What it’s like to work with us
TikTok Pixel and Events API questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: Do I need the TikTok Events API?
items.answer: For most online stores, yes. The Pixel misses conversions in the browser, especially in TikTok’s in-app browser; the Events API sends them from your server.

items.question: How do I set up the TikTok Events API on Shopify?
items.answer: Shopify’s TikTok app can send events server-side. We check it’s on, deduplicated and sending the right values.

items.question: How does deduplication work on TikTok?
items.answer: When the Pixel and the Events API send the same event, both include the same event ID. TikTok keeps one and discards the duplicate.

items.question: Why doesn’t TikTok show the same sales as my store?
items.answer: Usually because only the Pixel is installed, the click ID is lost at checkout, or purchases are counted twice. Attribution windows also differ, so some gap is normal.

items.question: Should my campaigns optimise for purchases?
items.answer: Yes, once TikTok sees enough purchases, usually around 50 a week per campaign. Good tracking is what gets you there.

items.question: Is the Events API allowed under privacy laws?
items.answer: Yes, when it respects consent and customer data is hashed before it is sent. We set it up to follow your cookie banner.
